synthetic fixture label and changed only the fixture; it is actually the exact
catalogue key, so that broke lookup and attachment traversal.

The existing catalogue item now uses `belt`, displays as

existing traversal assertions. Serialized IDs, catalogue revision and hashes

`ac20b9205127f71d1e114125872502bd8a1e9491`,
including the unchanged attachment-traversal assertion.
The PR records the remaining broader acceptance limits.

**Put occupancy and its payload into `PreviewTarget`.** Both preview producers emit empty attachment capacity, an occupied attachment, or an occupied unattached item. The two neighboring enums also admit `Empty + Detached`, and `entity` changes meaning between a parent and an item. Please express the alternatives together, for example `EmptyAttachment { parent } | Occupied { entity, attachment: PreviewAttachment }`, retaining the attached/unattached distinction only for an occupied item. Preserve ordering, depth-based capacity selection and the occupied fallback for unavailable item definitions. This is state consolidation, not a request to derive the Boolean mapping through Serde. See the [state-role rule](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/f0ba1326179fae1c345f83aa31ded5529ee5cd87/crates/AGENTS.md#L58-L65).

**Express the canonical-reference requirement in this lookup's input contract.** `file_for` accepts arbitrary `&ItemDefinition`/`&EquipmentPlacement` but compares their addresses. An equivalent cloned definition and its matching placement therefore return `None`, although their IDs select an admitted asset. The current tactical caller resolves canonical references first, so this is an API-envelope weakness rather than an observed lookup failure. Admit a canonical catalogue item/placement handle at the lookup boundary and accept that handle here, or resolve stable identity within the owner. Don't merely switch these parameters to `&'static`: that still doesn't prove catalogue provenance. Preserve placement-parent membership and the existing sorted default-placement choice. See the [single-owner and typed-boundary rules](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/28a593c7613cfcf7b348a550c6acca1d7e40a16c/crates/AGENTS.md#L31-L54).

**Own the rule and its required landmarks together.** `FrameLandmark::Unused` usefully removes a raw zero sentinel, but `rule` and the six independently writable slots still permit combinations such as `Rule::Foot` with unused required foot/ball slots. `device_word` then silently encodes those as joint zero. Prefer a payload-bearing frame-landmark enum with named required `RigJointOrdinal` fields per rule, deriving the rule tag and six-word layout only in the existing uniform packer. A private checked aggregate is also sufficient if it rejects missing required slots. Preserve intentional repeated landmarks, central/paired side semantics, slot order, tags and unused-zero encoding. Current builders fill the slots deliberately; this is an incomplete aggregate envelope, not a demonstrated fitting regression. See the [record and closed-role guidance](https://github.com/adventure-simulator-group/fabelgeist/blob/28a593c7613cfcf7b348a550c6acca1d7e40a16c/crates/AGENTS.md#L43-L65).
